name: Finnish Social Security number
issuer: the Digital and Population Data Services Agency
note: Finland's sheet (its government's own sheet on the OECD's automatic-exchange portal ('Information on Tax Identification Numbers'; the OECD's index page sits behind a bot check and wasn't opened, the sheet itself came straight back)), read 2026-10-30: the TIN is the Finnish Social Security number, given at birth or on immigrating by the Digital and Population Data Services Agency; 11 characters: six digits of the birth date, a century sign (+ for the 1800s; - or Y, X, W, V, U for the 1900s; A to F from 2000), three digits and a final alphanumeric character (its rule isn't given, `check` left out). Read as given at birth, to residents. No fee or time is stated.

sources.title: OECD AEOI portal, Finland: Information on Tax Identification Numbers (the jurisdiction's own sheet)
sources.said: The TIN is the Finnish Social Security number, given at birth or when immigrating by the Digital and Population Data Services Agency. ... For individuals, it consists of 11 characters: - 6 digits - 1 character which can be + (plus), - (minus) or the letter Y, X, W, V, U, A, B, C, D, E, F - 3 digits - 1 alphanumeric character
